text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000079 bills 99215 well above expected in every complexity band, including on sampled low-complexity visits with minor diagnoses, but records for only two 99215 claims came back, too few to judge.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess is not explained by a sicker panel alone. This provider's 99215 share exceeds the all-provider share in every condition band, roughly two to three times higher in each. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include visits coded only with follow-up, rash, upper respiratory infection or back pain diagnoses (e.g., C0037858, C0037894, C0038272, C0038550), which is a pattern consistent with upcoding. Against that, both documented 99215 claims (C0038129, C0038635) were supported at high MDM, and only one documented claim overall (C0037804, a 99214) fell below the billed level. Only 1.6% of claims have records, so the documentation is too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled 99215 claims on patients with no chronic conditions and only minor diagnoses, to see whether high-complexity MDM or time is genuinely documented and not cloned."}
